current_text.html: When the offense with which an accused person stands charged took place at a distance, and it is inconvenient for the witnesses to appear before the court having jurisdiction, that court may either (a) appoint a commission of its body, or (b) request the coordinate court contiguous to the place where the facts occurred to take the testimony for it, or (c) have the testimony taken by videoconference, which shall employ technical means that ensure that all persons participating in the meeting can see and hear each other at the same time, and which allows for live cross-examination by both parties. The accused shall always have reasonable notice of the time and place of the meeting of this commission or coordinate court.

metadata.summary: A Houston Metro Presbytery overture to amend BCO 32-8 to allow video testimony by witnesses in church judicial proceedings was found in conflict and adopted by the CCB.

occurrences.excerpt: …witnesses shall be examined in the presence of the accused (as permitted by BCO 32-8), or at least after he shall have received due citation to attend. Witnesses may be cross-examined by both parties, and any questions asked must be pertinent to the issue.

metadata.synopsis: An elder appealed Presbytery’s elevation, without additional process, of suspensions from office and the Sacraments to deposition and excommunication. The SJC granted the appeal, reversed in whole, and remanded, restoring the prior suspensions. Elevation required a hearing on incorrigibility and contumacy—with a charge, evidence, plea, and defense—but not a full de novo trial; disagreement with the original verdict alone was insufficient. The SJC left unresolved deposition from office when excommunication is absent.

relationships.title: Herron et al. v. Central Indiana Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: Herron and others challenged Presbytery’s decision to proceed to trial after a BCO 31-2 finding, his administrative suspension, denial of access to Presbytery records and meetings, and a public statement. The SJC sustained only the access issue: suspension from official functions did not remove his membership rights, though it did not entitle him to every investigative-committee document. Finding no clear error on the other issues, it ordered trial to proceed, temporarily stayed censure decisions, and postponed related complaints through trial and any appeal.

A minister appealed a judgment finding him guilty on most charges and imposing six months’ suspension. The SJC held BCO 32-20 barred Specifications 1, 2, and 4 because Presbytery lacked extraordinary justification for prosecuting old allegations, but did not bar ongoing Specification 3. It separately found the entire process constitutionally flawed and prejudicial. The SJC reversed the whole censure, declined Presbytery’s requested harsher sentence, and concluded the matter. A concurrence disputed the majority’s BCO 32-20 interpretation while agreeing with the result.

A complainant challenged Nashville Presbytery's handling of allegations against a teaching elder. The SJC held the matter judicially out of order and dismissed it, finding the original filing with the church session was not a BCO 43-1 complaint because the session lacked jurisdiction over the teaching elder. Presbytery properly treated the allegations as BCO 31-2/34-1 reports, and the complainant, not a Nashville member, lacked standing to complain about that new action. A nine-member dissent argued the filing of charges conferred standing under prior SJC cases.

A teaching elder appealed his judgment and deposition for refusing Presbytery committee directives and allegedly avoiding accountability. The SJC sustained five of nine specifications, holding that the committee could not impose requirements lacking constitutional warrant or control an independent mission board; vague allegations and testimony unavailable for cross-examination also impaired the trial. Because the record did not prove an ongoing pattern of insubordination, it vacated the censure and remanded for a constitutionally compliant proceeding or dismissal. Three specifications failed, while one duplicated another.
